claims.statement: URE's 2024 report records 5,980 renewable-source connection refusals across the five major distribution operators for applications filed in 2024 or earlier, with solar representing most recorded refusals; this is direct evidence that pre-application selection is a costly workflow rather than a theoretical inconvenience.

The European Commission's PVGIS already supplies location-specific solar-resource and production estimates, so a prototype can obtain a credible public generation baseline without buying satellite data.

Hypothesis: an installer will pay 2,500 PLN for a preflight when one avoided low-probability engineering submission or a better-selected parcel is worth materially more; this willingness-to-pay has not been validated.

contrary_evidence: Experienced developers already use grid engineers and informal DSO knowledge, so a score based mainly on public statistics would be too shallow.
Granular refusal and successful-connection outcomes may be unavailable or contractually restricted, preventing the proposed data moat.

economics.acquisition_route: Prove five cases inside the family business, then bundle trials through wholesalers and grid engineers who already reach installers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: reach 20 paid teams and roughly 0.5M PLN ARR in year 1, 120 teams at a 35k PLN blended ARR in year 3, and about 2M PLN EBITDA by year 6. At 4x EBITDA and 65% founder ownership, business equity would be about 5.2M PLN; the path fails if outcome data never becomes granular.
economics.founder_time: 12 to 18 hours weekly for a six-month MVP and dataset partnerships, within the five-hours-per-day ceiling
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 80% to 90% after automated public-data ingestion and bounded expert review; early bespoke engineering is excluded
economics.payback: Buyer hypothesis: one avoided weak application or one improved site choice repays several reports; founder CAC should repay within three reports from a referred account
economics.pricing: 2,500 PLN per standard preflight; 24,000 to 60,000 PLN per year for team workflow and benchmarks
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every new parcel creates a repeat event, while DSO updates and portfolio benchmarking support annual renewal

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A consented parcel-by-DSO outcome graph linking document features, requested capacity, refusal reason, amendment, and eventual connection
fingerprint.customer: Polish C&I PV and battery installers and small project developers pursuing 50 kW to 5 MW sites
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Family-installer beachhead, electrical wholesalers, grid-engineering partners, and downloadable benchmark reports aimed at DSO territories
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: 2,500 PLN decision report or 24,000 to 60,000 PLN annual team subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer or developer pays when ordering a parcel preflight or renewing a pipeline intelligence seat
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A parcel enters the development pipeline and the team must decide whether to fund grid-connection engineering and an application

founder_fit: Strong fit with the founder's data-science skills, Polish location, low-social-energy product preference, and direct access to a seven-person renewable installer for workflow observation and early cases. A useful prototype can run part-time and without founder-led video marketing.
risks: Customers could treat a probabilistic score as engineering or legal assurance.
Outcome data may contain commercially sensitive parcel information and require strict access controls.
DSO process changes can make learned patterns stale.

structure.control_point: The go-or-no-go record created before grid-connection engineering spend
structure.critical_dependency: Lawful access to enough granular successful and refused application outcomes to produce lift beyond a checklist

thesis: Build a paid parcel-and-DSO preflight for 50 kW to 5 MW solar and battery projects. It would combine public refusal statistics, voluntarily contributed application outcomes, document-completeness checks, and PV yield baselines to rank plausible connection paths before a developer buys a full engineering package. The initial beachhead is installers in ENEA, ENERGA, and PGE territories, seeded through the founder's family renewable-energy company; the score is explicitly a probability estimate, never a promise of connection.
title: DSO Refusal Atlas for Polish C&I Solar and Storage
uncertainties: Whether twenty installers will contribute outcome data in exchange for credits or benchmarks.
Whether a parcel-level model can outperform a simple DSO-territory checklist without confidential grid data.
The actual spend wasted per rejected application and the point at which developers authorize preflight spend.
